text: The man lived among the tombs.
People had tried to help him, then feared him, then stayed away.
Help was already coming.
The man had been hurting for a long time.
Evil had taken hold of him and torn his life apart.
He could not live safely in his home or rest among his people.
Others had tried chains, but the chains did not hold.
That changed everything.
The man ran toward Jesus.
It did not look peaceful.
Not for Jesus.
Jesus did not run from him.
Others had feared the man.
He knew what was holding the man, and He had power over it.
The evil begged.
That alone tells the story.
The man had been tormented for years.
The evil was not stronger than Jesus.
Jesus spoke, and evil had to obey.
The change was terrible and sudden.
The evil left the man, and the scene broke open with force.
Jesus had set him free.
When the people came, they saw the man sitting there.
That may have been the most shocking part.
He was sitting near Jesus, clothed, clear-minded, and free.
The people knew what he had been.
They knew the fear, the noise in the night, the shame around his name.
The way everyone had learned to avoid him.
Now they saw him changed.
So they asked Jesus to leave.
The healed man wanted to go with Jesus.
That made sense.
The man had a story now, and his home needed to hear it.
The man left the tombs behind.
He walked toward home as a different man.
Jesus had sent him.
The man did not need a long sermon.
He had his own life as proof.
His family could look at him and see the mercy of God.
His neighbors could hear his voice calm and clear.
The man was free.
The tombs were not his home anymore.
Fear was not his name anymore.
Now he was alive, and he was going home.
